data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Both architectures are equally vulnerable to the worst-case correlated failure; decentralized networks merely obscure the correlation until a shared cause is found, while large services make the coupling explicit and thus auditable.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Decentralized operators demonstrably use non-overlapping supply chains","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service's internal coupling is not actually modeled or monitored","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Independence is verified by active stress injection rather than assumed from topology","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If a single root cause can fail one service, it can fail all services sharing the causal dependency (e.g., a global DNS provider, TLS certificate authority, or BGP route). In a large system, the internal coupling is explicit and can be modeled (e.g., 'all replicas depend on the same configuration service'), exposing the correlated failure mode to analysis. In a decentralized network, the causal chain is hidden across organizational boundaries, making the system appear independent until the shared dependency fails simultaneously, preventing proactive mitigation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
